role: ADR 004: explains why every quality rule is a numeric ceiling in .ci/*.txt that may only decrease, enforced by check_budget_monotonicity.sh.

units.does: no behavioural claim: ADR title 'Debt is ratcheted, never waived'.

units.key: § 004 — Debt is ratcheted, never waived > Context
units.does: Claims every quality rule (SwiftLint warnings, .shared uses, try? uses, ObservableObject conformances, fixed-point fonts, test skips, aggregate type size) has a numeric ceiling in .ci/*.txt. Verified: .ci/ holds swiftlint_warning_budget.txt (81), shared_usage_budget.txt (90), try_optional_budget.txt (170), legacy_observable_object_budget.txt (0), fixed_font_budget.txt (13), test_skip_budget.txt (9), aggregate_type_size_budget.txt (0).

units.key: § 004 — Debt is ratcheted, never waived > Decision
units.does: Claims ceilings only move down and min_* floors only up: check_budget_monotonicity.sh compares every numeric (whole or decimal, read_number) .ci/*.txt with the baseline and fails on a loosening (raise, floor lowered, deleted or non-numeric budget) lacking a 'budget-raise-ok:' trailer in the compared range; baseline is the PR target or, on push, github.event.before so every pushed commit is in range, falling back to HEAD~1 with a message only when that tip is missing; zero swiftlint:disable in Emuqu/Sources; refactor-spec gate counts justified exceptions separately.

units.key: § 004 — Debt is ratcheted, never waived > Why not a hard zero
units.does: Argues against aspirational hard-zero gates: a coverage gate requiring a figure the suite cannot reach never passes, so nobody runs it, while the docs keep stating the figure; a measured ceiling blocks regression and only moves one way. Current coverage floors are .ci/min_coverage.txt 44, min_coverage_logic.txt 45, min_coverage_views.txt 43.5; no 90% figure remains in README.md or docs/runbooks.

units.key: § 004 — Debt is ratcheted, never waived > Consequence
units.does: Claims the .ci numbers are a debt inventory, the honest measure of what is still outstanding, and that the ceilings are debt inventories rather than assurance targets.
